question: is a gen1 flight-line vertical tie a property of the LINE, or of the place it was fitted?

inputs.role: gen1 tile over the Elba study area, for the window ladder
gen1 tile over the Elba study area, for the window ladder

params.name: res_m
params.why: coreg.coregister_swaths / align_swaths default grid resolution (2.0 m)

params.name: exclude
params.why: coreg.coregister_swaths terrain proxy ~isin(classification,(5,6,9)) -- the VENDOR classes, so no CSF run is needed

params.name: tie_modes
params.why: the two estimators coreg.coregister_swaths supports; corrections_geoid.json records swath_tie='intercept' as the pipeline's

params.name: half_width_m
params.why: window half-width for the along-track sweep and the chains. There is NO library default and none is invented here; 400 m is one rung of the ladder in section 2, chosen so the window fits inside a single 2.5 km tile at every along-track sample. Section 2 measures what the choice costs; section 3 is re-runnable at any other rung with --half-width-m

params.name: ladder_half_widths_m
params.why: the window sizes reported in section 2. Chosen to span a factor of 12, from below one flight-line sidelap width to a whole tile; nothing is excluded on their basis, the whole ladder is printed

params.name: shape
params.why: square window. A disk would give a ragged grid edge and fewer cells for the same half-width; localtie supports both and --shape switches it

params.name: mark_radius_m
params.why: radius within which a mark's flight line is identified by return count (groundtruth.chain.covering_lines). It selects WHICH LINE the mark is on, not which marks are used; every mark is reported

params.name: target_line
params.why: the frame the marks are carried into. 137 is the middle Elba line and the one the brief names; --target-line changes it

columns.pair: flight-line pair, ref-src; dz is added to src to reach ref's frame
columns.tie_mode: which coreg tie estimator: overlap_median or intercept
columns.half_width_m: window half-width about the stated location, m
columns.dz_mm: the tie, from coreg.coregister_swaths in the stated tie mode, mm
columns.dz_median_mm: independent check: median of the UNSHIFTED overlap difference, mm
columns.nk_cells: cells the Nuth & Kaeaeb fit used; 0 means the fit was abandoned
columns.ovl_cells: cells where both lines have terrain returns in this window
columns.nmad1_mm: robust scatter left in the overlap after the tie, mm
columns.degenerate: YES when the N&K fit used zero cells (dz is then coreg's 0.0)
